title: Arts and Culture
description: Ten short stories about people who make and enjoy art: a voice class, a day at a museum, a book club, a community theater, a street artist, a short film, a drawing class, a big work of art, an arts center and a holiday concert.

lessons.title: A Song for Mom's Birthday
lessons.summary: Nora, an engineer, takes a voice class so she can sing at her mother's birthday party.
lessons.text:
Nora is 34 years old, and she is an engineer. She works for a large engineering company in Denver. She likes engineering, but it is not her only interest. She has loved music since she was a little girl.

In 2 months, Nora's mother is going to celebrate her 60th birthday. Nora wants to give her a special present: a song. Her mother's favorite song is an old love song, and Nora wants to sing it at the birthday party. But there is one problem. Nora has never sung in front of other people.

So Nora looks for a voice teacher. She finds Mr. Alvarez, who teaches in a small room above a music store near her office. His fee is $40 an hour. "The fee is not low," Nora thinks, "but my mother is worth it."

At the first class, Mr. Alvarez listens to Nora. "You have a nice voice," he says. "But your technique is weak. Good technique is extremely important, because it protects your voice."

Then he shows her a simple technique. "Hold 2 fingers in front of your mouth," he says. "When you sing, you should feel only a little air on your fingers. If you feel a lot of air, you are using too much."

After that, he asks, "Do you prefer to practice in the morning or in the evening?"
"I prefer the evening," Nora says. "I'm an engineer, so I'm at work all day."
"That's fine," he says. "But you have to practice every day. If you practice for 20 minutes every evening, you will be ready for the party."

So Nora starts to prepare for the party. Every evening after work, she practices the song. Some evenings she is extremely tired, but she never stops.

The birthday party is held in a small restaurant. Nora is afraid at first, but she remembers her teacher's technique. She sings the old love song from the beginning to the end. Her mother cries, and everyone in the restaurant stands up. Later, her mother says that she is very proud of her. Nora is proud of herself, too.

Questions:
What does Nora do?
Nora is an engineer at a large engineering company in Denver.
Why does Nora look for a voice teacher?
She wants to sing her mother's favorite song at her mother's 60th birthday party.
What is Mr. Alvarez's fee?
His fee is $40 an hour.
When does Nora prefer to practice, and why?
She prefers the evening, because she is at work all day.
How does Nora prepare for the party?
She practices the song every evening after work.
What does her mother say after the song?
She says that she is very proud of Nora.

lessons.title: A Hunt at the Museum
lessons.summary: Walter takes his granddaughter Mia to an old museum, where she looks for 8 objects in a picture hunt.
lessons.text:
Walter is 72 years old. Every summer, he takes his granddaughter Mia to the City Museum of Art and History. The museum is an old institution. It was opened in 1890, and it is one of the oldest institutions in the city.

This year, Mia is 10. When they arrive, a young woman at the door gives Mia a piece of paper. "This is our picture hunt," she says. "On this paper, there are 8 small pictures of objects in the museum. If you find all 8 objects, you will get a gift at the end."

The first room is about religion. It shows art from many different religions: old books, small figures of wood and glass windows in many colors. Next to every object, there is a short description on a card. Walter reads every description to Mia. One description says that a book in the room is very rare. "Only 3 books like this one exist in the world," Walter reads. "Rare means that there are very few of something," he explains.

In the second room, Mia finds the first object from the hunt: a silver cup. The cup was made in the mid-1700s. "Mid means middle," Walter explains. "So the cup was made around 1750."

The third room is full of iron objects: iron tools, iron doors and a giant iron key. It is the biggest key that Mia has ever seen. It is even bigger than Walter! Mia finds 6 more objects from the hunt in this room.

In the last room, Mia looks for the last object, a picture of a ship. But she can't find it. There is an empty space on the wall. A small card says: "This picture has been removed for cleaning. It will return in mid September." Mia is sad. Then a guard comes to her. "The picture was removed, so nobody can find it this week," he says. "You can still get your gift."

At the end, Mia gets her gift: a small silver key ring. "This was the best hunt ever," she says.

Questions:
When was the museum opened?
It was opened in 1890.
What does Mia get at the door?
She gets a piece of paper for the picture hunt.
What does the word "rare" mean?
Rare means that there are very few of something.
When was the silver cup made?
It was made in the mid-1700s, around 1750.
What is in the third room?
The third room is full of iron objects: iron tools, iron doors and a giant iron key.
Why can't Mia find the last object?
She can't find it because the picture was removed for cleaning.

lessons.title: An Email from the Book Club
lessons.summary: Anna writes to her book club about their last meeting and the special guest who is coming next time.
lessons.text:
Dear friends,

Thank you all for coming to our book club meeting last Thursday. I think it was our best meeting this year. We talked for almost 3 hours! Thank you also to Paul, who made dinner for all of us. The dinner was excellent.

For anyone who missed the meeting, here is a short report. We discussed the first 10 chapters of "The Long Winter Road" by Helen Marsh. The book is about 2 sisters who own a farm together. The main conflict of the story is between the sisters. The older sister wants to sell the farm, but the younger sister wants to keep it.

We had a long debate about the sisters. Some of us blamed the older sister for the conflict. Others said that the younger sister was to blame, because she never listens. Paul had a strong argument for the older sister: she has 3 children, and she needs the money. Rita had a strong argument for the younger sister: the farm has been in their family for 100 years. It was a good debate, and nobody got angry. That is what I love about our club.

Now some news. At our next meeting, we will have a special guest. Helen Marsh, the author of the book, is going to visit us! Apparently, she lives only 30 minutes from here. My sister knows her, and my sister asked her to visit us. Apparently, Ms. Marsh loves small book clubs. She said she would be happy to come.

Our guest will answer our questions, so please prepare 1 or 2 questions for her. Before the meeting, you should read chapters 11 to 20. If you don't finish those chapters, you might not understand everything she says about the ending.

The meeting will be at my house on Thursday, May 14, at 7 in the evening. I will make dinner this time. If you can come, please reply to this email by Monday. If there is any food you can't eat, please tell me in your reply.

See you soon!
Anna

Questions:
How does Anna's email begin?
It begins with the words "Dear friends."
Who made dinner at the last meeting?
Paul made dinner for everyone.
What is the main conflict of the story?
The main conflict is between the 2 sisters. The older sister wants to sell the farm, but the younger sister wants to keep it.
What was Paul's argument?
His argument was that the older sister has 3 children and needs the money.
Who is the special guest at the next meeting?
The guest is Helen Marsh, the author of the book.
Which chapters should the members read, and when should they reply?
They should read chapters 11 to 20, and they should reply by Monday.

lessons.title: My First Time on Stage
lessons.summary: Kate, a nurse, joins a community theater group and plays a witness in a court play.
lessons.text:
My name is Kate, and I have worked as a nurse at the hospital in Fairview for 12 years. My shifts are long, and sometimes I work night shifts. Last spring, my friend Dana asked me to join the Fairview Community Players, a small theater group in our town. "You should try it," she said. "You might love it." I said I didn't have time, but finally I agreed.

The group was preparing a play about a court case. The theme of the play was the truth. In the play, a young man is in court because people think he took money from the company where he works. He denies it. His lawyer has to defend him.

At first, I only helped with the lights. Everyone was kind, and I felt that I belonged there. After 2 weeks, I felt like I belonged to a second family.

Then, 3 weeks before the show, there was a shock. The woman who played the most important witness became ill. She was very ill, and her doctor said she couldn't perform. The director looked at me. "You know the play," she said. "Can you play the witness?" I was shocked, because I was not an actor. But I said yes.

For 3 weeks, I practiced my lines after every shift. In the play, the witness tells the court what she saw. The lawyer wants to defend the young man, so he asks the witness many hard questions. The young man denies everything, but the witness doesn't change her story.

On the night of the show, the hall was full. The audience was big: almost 200 people. My appearance on stage was only 10 minutes long, but I was very afraid. Then I started to speak, and I forgot about the audience.

At the end, the whole audience stood up and cheered. The next day, a local newspaper said that my appearance as the witness was one of the best parts of the night. Now I'm preparing for my second show.

Questions:
Where does Kate work?
She works as a nurse at the hospital in Fairview.
What was the theme of the play?
The theme of the play was the truth.
How did Kate feel in the group?
She felt that she belonged there, like in a second family.
Why did Kate have to play the witness?
She had to play the witness because the woman who played the witness became ill.
How big was the audience?
The audience was almost 200 people.
What did the newspaper say?
The newspaper said that her appearance as the witness was one of the best parts of the night.

lessons.title: The Wall on Oak Street
lessons.summary: Leo, a street artist, makes a big picture of a forest on the wall of a library with help from the neighbors.
lessons.text:
Leo is a street artist in Austin. He makes large pictures on the walls of buildings. He likes to fill plain walls with color. He drives an old blue van, and the van is always full of paint and tools.

Leo has a variety of clients. Some of his clients are shops and restaurants. Others are schools and hospitals. Last month, he got a new client: the Oak Street Library. The library wanted a picture on its long side wall.

Before Leo starts a job, he has to obtain permission from the city. Sometimes it takes months to obtain permission, but this time the library obtained it in only 1 week.

Then Leo talked to the children at the library. He asked them what they wanted to see on the wall. The children gave him a variety of ideas: animals, trees, books and stars. Leo decided to make a forest under a night sky. A path would go through the forest, and children with books in their hands would walk on the path.

Working on a high wall can be dangerous. Leo always uses safety equipment. "This job is dangerous if you don't pay attention," he says.

For 3 weeks, Leo worked on the wall. First, he made the sky dark blue, with hundreds of small white stars. Then he used dark green to fill the whole bottom part of the wall with trees. Finally, he added the path and the children.

The library also asked the people on the street to contribute. Many people contributed money for the paint. Some children contributed, too: they drew small animals in the forest.

When the wall was finished, the library had a small party, and people came to see it. A little girl pointed at the sky in the picture and said, "Look, there's my star!" Leo smiled. For him, that was the best part of the job.

Questions:
What does Leo drive?
He drives an old blue van that is full of paint and tools.
Who are Leo's clients?
He has a variety of clients, such as shops, restaurants, schools and hospitals.
What does Leo have to obtain before he starts a job?
He has to obtain permission from the city.
What did Leo decide to make on the wall?
He decided to make a forest under a night sky, with a path through the forest.
How did Leo fill the bottom part of the wall?
He used dark green to fill it with trees.
How did the people on the street contribute?
Many people contributed money for the paint, and some children drew small animals in the forest.

lessons.title: Maya's First Film
lessons.summary: Maya, a young film school graduate, makes a short film for a film competition.
lessons.text:
Maya graduated from film school in June. Right after she graduated, she wanted to make her first short film. She had a small camera, an old computer and 3 friends who wanted to help.

Then Maya saw an ad for a short film competition in her city. The competition had 3 requirements. The first requirement was the length: films had to be a minimum of 5 minutes and a maximum of 15 minutes. The second requirement was the date: films had to arrive before October 1. The third requirement was a short letter about the film. The letter had to be sent by mail, not by email.

Maya wrote a simple story about an old man and his dog. The shooting was planned for 4 days. On the first day, they wanted to shoot by the lake, but there was heavy rain. "We can't shoot in the rain," Maya said. They waited in the car for 2 hours. When the rain stopped, they started the shooting.

After 4 days, Maya had almost 3 hours of film. Now she had to make it 15 minutes long. She used free software on her old computer. The software was slow, and it crashed many times. One night, it crashed and she lost 2 hours of work. Maya almost cried. "This film is going to be a failure," she said to her friend.

"It won't be a failure," her friend Tom said. "You should save your work every 10 minutes. That's all."

Maya followed Tom's advice. After 3 weeks, the film was ready. It was 12 minutes long, so it was longer than the minimum. Maya wrote the letter and sent it by mail. Then she sent the film online.

In November, Maya got a letter in the mail. Her film was chosen for the competition! It was shown in a small movie theater with 9 other films. It didn't win, but people liked it very much. After the show, a man told her that the old man and his dog made him cry. Maya was very happy.

Questions:
When did Maya graduate from film school?
She graduated in June.
What were the 3 requirements of the competition?
The film had to be a minimum of 5 minutes and a maximum of 15 minutes, it had to arrive before October 1, and a letter had to be sent by mail.
Why couldn't they shoot on the first day?
They couldn't shoot because there was heavy rain.
What happened to the software?
The software was slow, and it crashed many times.
What advice did Tom give her?
He said she should save her work every 10 minutes.
What happened in November?
Maya got a letter in the mail, and her film was chosen for the competition.

lessons.title: Apples, Eggs and an Old Shoe
lessons.summary: Rosa, who is 68, takes a drawing class and learns to draw a simple group of objects.
lessons.text:
Rosa is 68 years old. She has always wanted to learn to draw, but she never had time. Now she is retired, so she takes a drawing class at the community center. The class is every Tuesday from 6 till 8 in the evening.

At the first class, the teacher, Mr. Kim, puts some objects on a table: a bowl with 3 red apples, 2 white eggs, an empty wine bottle and an old brown shoe. "Today, you will draw these objects," he says. "A picture of objects that don't move is called a still life."

First, Mr. Kim shows the class some samples. The samples are drawings by his old students. In one sample, the apples look so real that Rosa wants to eat them.

Then the students start. Rosa begins with the bowl and the apples. After an hour, she looks at her drawing. The apples don't look round. They look flat, like circles on the paper. The eggs look flat, too. The wine bottle is fine, but the shoe is too big.

Rosa starts to have negative thoughts. "I'm too old for this," she thinks. "I will never learn."

Mr. Kim walks over to her. "Your drawing is a good start," he says. "If you make one side of the apple darker, it won't look flat anymore. Try it." Rosa makes the left side of each apple darker. Suddenly, the apples look round!

"And there is one more thing," Mr. Kim says. "Every student has a negative voice in their head. You should ignore it. If you ignore it, you will learn faster."

Rosa stays till the end of the class. At home, she puts an apple and an egg in a bowl and draws them again. She practices every day. After 2 months, her drawing of the bowl, the apples, the eggs, the wine bottle and the shoe is very good. Mr. Kim asks if he can use it as a sample for his new students. Rosa says yes. She is very happy.

Questions:
When is the drawing class?
It is every Tuesday from 6 till 8 in the evening.
What objects does Mr. Kim put on the table?
He puts a bowl with 3 apples, 2 eggs, an empty wine bottle and an old shoe on the table.
What are the samples?
The samples are drawings by Mr. Kim's old students.
What is the problem with Rosa's first drawing?
The apples and the eggs look flat.
What does Mr. Kim say about the negative voice?
He says that she should ignore it.
What does Mr. Kim ask after 2 months?
He asks if he can use her drawing as a sample for his new students.

lessons.title: A Metal Horse for Bayport
lessons.summary: Sam, a truck driver, carefully moves a giant metal horse from the port to a new park.
lessons.text:
Bayport is a small city by the sea. Last year, a famous artist, Elena Cruz, made a work of art for the city: a giant metal horse. The horse is 20 feet high and very heavy. It was made in another country, and it was sent to Bayport by ship.

Sam is a truck driver. He works for a small transport company in Bayport. One morning, his boss, Linda, called him into her office. "I have a special task for you," she said. "The horse is arriving at the port tomorrow. Your task is to transport it from the port to the new park in the center of the city."

Sam was worried, because the horse was extremely heavy and the streets in the old center were not wide. "We can't have an accident," his boss said. "The city paid a lot of money for this horse. If there is an accident, everyone will hear about it."

That evening, Sam checked his truck and went to fill it with fuel. "I don't want to stop for fuel on the way," he said.

The next morning, the ship arrived at the port. A big machine lifted the horse off the ship. Then it put the horse on Sam's truck. Workers tied the horse to the truck, so it could not move.

Sam drove very slowly. People stood by the street and took photos of the horse on the truck. It took 2 hours to transport the horse 5 miles, but there was no accident.

At the park, the machine lifted the horse off the truck and put it in its place. A week later, the park was opened. The governor of the state came to the opening. In her speech, the governor said that the horse was a gift for everyone in Bayport.

After the speech, Linda found Sam. "That was a hard task," she said.
"It was indeed," Sam said. "But I'm proud of it."
"You should be. It was indeed a great day for our company," Linda said.

Questions:
What did Elena Cruz make for Bayport?
She made a giant metal horse.
What task did Linda give Sam?
His task was to transport the horse from the port to the new park.
Why did Sam fill the truck with fuel?
He didn't want to stop for fuel on the way.
How was the horse moved from the ship to the truck?
A big machine lifted it off the ship and put it on the truck.
What did the governor say in her speech?
The governor said that the horse was a gift for everyone in Bayport.

lessons.title: Good News at the Arts Center
lessons.summary: Frank, the chairman of an arts center, shares the results of a survey and some good news about money.
lessons.text:
The Greenville Arts Center is in an old school building. It has a small theater and 3 rooms for art classes. Every year in January, the members of the center's board meet to talk about the past year. The chairman of the board is Frank, a former teacher. Frank has been the chairman for 6 years.

This year, Frank began the meeting with a smile. "I have good news," he said. "Last fall, we did a survey. We asked the people who come to the center about their experience. More than 500 people answered the survey."

Then he showed the board some statistics from the survey. "These statistics are very interesting," he said. "90 percent of the people said they were happy with the center. 70 percent said they come here on a regular basis, at least once a month. And 40 percent said they found us on the internet."

Next, Frank talked about money. "Our revenue grew last year," he said. "Our revenue from tickets was $80,000. That is 20 percent more than the year before. One reason is our new online platform. People can now buy tickets on the platform at any time. Obviously, that is easier than coming to the center."

Then Frank shared the best news. "Last month, the state senate voted to give money to small arts centers," he said. "The state budget is about 30 billion dollars. Only a very small part of those billions goes to the arts, but we are going to get $50,000. The senate wants us to use the money for children's classes."

Lucy, a young member of the board, asked a question. "Should we start new classes, or should we make the old classes bigger?"

"That's a good question," Frank said. "Obviously, we can't decide everything today. I think we should meet on a weekly basis until we decide. If the survey shows that people want new classes, we will start new ones."

Everyone agreed, and the meeting ended.

Questions:
Who is Frank?
Frank is the chairman of the board of the Greenville Arts Center.
How many people answered the survey?
More than 500 people answered the survey.
What do the statistics say?
90 percent of the people are happy with the center, and 70 percent come on a regular basis.
Why did the revenue from tickets grow?
One reason is the new online platform, where people can buy tickets at any time.
What did the state senate do?
The senate voted to give money to small arts centers, and the center is going to get $50,000.
How often is the board going to meet?
The board is going to meet on a weekly basis until it decides.

lessons.title: Hana's Holiday Diary
lessons.summary: Hana, who is 13, writes in her diary about her music group, her new baby brother and the holiday concert.
lessons.text:
Monday, December 5
My name is Hana, and I am 13 years old. This is my fifth year in the Riverside music group for kids. I have been in the group since I was 8. Every year in December, we give a holiday concert at the Riverside library. This year is special for me, because I am going to sing a song alone. For years, I have had a desire to sing alone in front of people. Now my desire is going to come true.

Wednesday, December 7
I cycled to practice today. It was cold, but I love cycling. It only takes 15 minutes to cycle there. Our teacher, Ms. Park, listened to my song and said my voice was getting stronger. She said that if I keep practicing, I will be ready for the holiday concert.

Friday, December 9
Today Ms. Park talked about the bond between the members of a group. "When you make music together, you build a bond," she said. "That bond makes the music better." I think she is right. My best friend Ben and I met in the group in our first year, and now we have a strong bond.

Sunday, December 11
Big news: my little brother was born this morning! His birth was 2 weeks early, but he is healthy. Mom and Dad are at the hospital, and Grandma is staying with me. I'm a little worried that Mom and Dad will miss the concert because of the birth.

Saturday, December 17
The holiday concert was tonight! The library was full. When I started my song, my voice was a little weak, but then it got stronger. Mom came to the concert, and Dad stayed at home with the baby. After the concert, Mom gave me a kiss and said she was proud of me. Then Grandma kissed me, too. It was my fifth holiday concert, but it was the best one.

Questions:
How long has Hana been in the music group?
She has been in the group since she was 8. This is her fifth year.
What desire has Hana had for years?
She has had a desire to sing alone in front of people.
How does Hana get to practice?
She cycles there. It takes 15 minutes.
What did Ms. Park say about the bond between the members?
She said that the bond makes the music better.
What happened on Sunday, December 11?
Hana's little brother was born. His birth was 2 weeks early.
What did Mom do after the concert?
She gave Hana a kiss and said she was proud of her.
